event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: CDNS’s February 13 2023 Form 10-K frames COVID-19 as a still-present, multi-faceted risk.  Because the pandemic is less than three years old, the Time-Decay principle allows high risk scores where warranted.  The filing blends forward-looking cautions with acknowledgements of concrete, albeit un-quantified, impacts that the company has already felt—inefficiencies, delivery delays, extra costs and volatile demand.  It also warns of broader macro-economic knock-on effects such as extended downturns, inflation and credit-collection issues.  However, management simultaneously discloses that, to date, COVID-19 “has not had a material, adverse impact” and that mitigation measures (remote-work protocols, policy adaptations) have sustained operations.  Overall, the evidence supports a medium-high residual risk: the pandemic is ongoing and continues to threaten supply chains, labour availability and customer demand, but the absence of material financial damage thus far, plus stated mitigation actions, temper the severity.  Scores therefore cluster in the 3-6 range rather than the extreme upper bound allowed for recent events.

evidence_list.snippet: Uncertainty caused by the recent challenging global political and economic conditions, including the effects of the recent rise in inflation and interest rates, the Russian invasion of Ukraine and the continuing COVID-19 pandemic, adverse changes to international trade relationships between countries in which we do business, protectionist measures or future decline in corporate or consumer spending could negatively impact our customers’ businesses, reducing the number of new chip designs and their overall research and development spending, including their spending on our products and services, and as a result decrease demand for our products and services.

components.reason: Explicitly cites the ‘continuing COVID-19 pandemic’ as part of a cluster of macro threats.
Connects pandemic-driven uncertainty to reduced customer R&D and hence lower demand for CDNS products.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Links COVID-19 to decreased customer spending and demand but does so in a broad list of factors; moderate risk indicator.

evidence_list.snippet: The ongoing COVID-19 pandemic could continue to adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.

components.reason: Direct statement that the pandemic is ‘ongoing’ and may ‘continue to adversely affect’ core financial metrics.
Covers multiple impact dimensions (business operations, results, financial condition).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Clear, forward-looking warning with broad scope; no mitigation mentioned, so risk is pronounced.

evidence_list.snippet: We are unable to accurately predict the full impact that the COVID-19 pandemic will have on our results of operations, financial condition, liquidity and cash flows due to numerous uncertainties, including the duration and severity of the pandemic, the impact of COVID-19 variants and the effects of containment measures.

components.reason: Highlights uncertainty and lack of visibility into future pandemic impacts.
Lists concrete uncertainty drivers (variants, containment measures, duration).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Emphasises unpredictability, increasing perceived risk though still generic and unquantified.

evidence_list.snippet: Our business and operations, as well as that of our customers, suppliers, contract manufacturers and other counterparties, could continue to be disrupted for an indefinite period of time.

components.reason: Warns of continuing disruption to CDNS operations.
Extends disruption risk to customers, suppliers, and manufacturers—broadening supply-chain concern.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Indefinite operational and supply-chain disruption elevates risk to upper-medium level.

evidence_list.snippet: As a result of the pandemic, we have experienced, and may continue to experience, inefficiencies, delays and additional costs in our product development, business operations and hardware product deliveries, as well as volatility in the demand for our products and services and the availability of supplies.

components.reason: Confirms actual experienced impacts (inefficiencies, delays, extra costs).
Specifies affected areas: product development, operations, hardware deliveries.
Notes demand volatility and supply availability issues—key pandemic hallmarks.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides concrete evidence of realised operational and supply-chain impacts, driving one of the highest risk scores.

evidence_list.snippet: The pandemic has also caused volatility in the financial markets and may increase the possibility of an extended global economic downturn and extended periods of high inflation, which could continue to affect demand for our products and services, our ability to collect payments from our customers and impact our results and financial condition.

components.reason: Links pandemic to macro-economic volatility and extended downturn/inflation.
Explains transmission mechanism to CDNS—lower demand and collection risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Connects pandemic to broader economic stressors that threaten revenue and cash collection.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, the pandemic has had, and may have, the effect of heightening many of the other risks described in this “Risk Factors” section.

components.reason: States pandemic amplifies multiple existing risks.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Acknowledges compounding effect but remains generic; yields lower mid-range score.

evidence_list.snippet: Since its inception, the COVID-19 pandemic has posed a variety of challenges to our day-to-day operations.
evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Identifies concrete operational strain, but without detail or quantification.

evidence_list.snippet: Despite these challenges, the pandemic has not had a material, adverse impact on our results of operations, financial condition, liquidity or cash flows.

components.reason: Explicit mitigation—no material adverse financial impact to date.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Strong mitigating statement neutralises prior risk signals for this sentence; net score set to zero.

evidence_list.snippet: While we are unable to accurately predict the full impact that COVID-19 and its continuing repercussions will have on our results of operations, financial condition, liquidity and cash flows, we have implemented policies and practices that have enabled us to support critical operations and execute our strategy.
evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Uncertainty adds minor risk but is outweighed by described mitigation steps, leading to a neutral score.
